headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist by default: Aci’s broad egress and CRM/email data can flow into Dify’s writable, server-side agent/tool environment.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aci can ingest and emit research, email, and CRM content, and Dify can read uploaded knowledge-base files and wire tools into agents/workflows. That creates a plausible instruction-hijack path if Aci output is copied into Dify or stored in shared files. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is not high.
conditions: IF Aci output is pasted into a Dify prompt or knowledge-base file
IF Dify treats uploaded file text as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Use a strict prompt delimiter around Aci output
Disable automatic ingestion of Aci-generated text into Dify prompts
Add a manual review step before any Dify tool call
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to imported content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aci touches CRM, email, calendar, support, and research data and has broad network egress. Dify reads uploaded files, stores conversation logs, and sends data to model providers and user-defined tools. If Aci outputs sensitive records into Dify, the pair can exfiltrate them beyond the original workspace by default.
conditions: IF Aci forwards CRM/email/support data into Dify inputs
IF Dify routes those inputs to model providers or OpenAPI tools
mitigations: Restrict Aci to non-sensitive records
Turn off or minimize Dify conversation logging
Block sensitive file uploads into Dify
Use separate credentials for Aci and Dify
requires-engineering: enforce DLP/redaction before handoff

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aci supports multiple instances and broad egress, while Dify supports multiple instances with shared state via its server datastore and server-side code-tool execution. Their write surfaces do not clearly overlap on the same directory, but they can contend over shared external resources such as APIs, CRM records, or datastore-backed workflows.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same CRM or workflow-backed record set
IF Dify workflows and Aci actions target the same external API without locking
mitigations: Assign disjoint resource ownership
Serialize writes through one orchestrator
Add per-record version checks
Use separate API credentials per agent
requires-engineering: implement distributed locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aci can generate CRM/email/calendar actions and Dify can execute tools and server-side code. If Dify consumes Aci output as authoritative, a mistaken or manipulated Aci result can cascade into downstream actions such as emails, API calls, or workflow updates. The pair lacks a documented verification barrier in the profiles.
conditions: IF Dify uses Aci output as the sole source for tool parameters
IF Dify workflows execute actions without human verification
mitigations: Require human approval before action tools run
Add schema validation on Aci outputs
Cross-check Aci facts against a second source
Limit Dify to read-only actions for Aci-fed workflows
requires-engineering: add confidence gating before execution

E_compliance.rationale: Aci touches email, CRM, customer support, and calendar data, while Dify stores conversation logs and uploaded knowledge-base files and sends data to model providers. That creates a plausible retention and residency mismatch for regulated customer data, even though no specific jurisdiction or certification gap is documented in either profile.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is routed from Aci into Dify logs or uploaded files
IF Dify retention settings exceed the organization’s policy for that data class
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from Dify inputs
Shorten Dify log retention
Review provider and tool data-processing terms
Tag sensitive records before transfer
requires-engineering: enforce residency and retention policy checks
